Dolutegravir and rilpivirine are indicated as a complete regimen to replace the current antiretroviral therapy (ART) in virologically suppressed adults who have no history of treatment failure and no known substitutions associated with resistance to dolutegravir or rilpivirine. Patients must have HIV-1 RNA levels <50 copies/mL on a stable ART regimen for at least 6 months. The recommended dose is one tablet (dolutegravir 50 mg/rilpivirine 25 mg) taken orally once daily. Pregnancy testing is recommended for patients with childbearing potential before initiating therapy. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been established in certain populations. 2. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 3. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 4. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as this may result in a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 5. Dexlansoprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 6. Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 7. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals, including rilpivirine. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 9. Esomeprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 10. Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 11. Fosphenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 12. Lansoprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 13. Nevirapine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 14. Omeprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 15. Oxcarbazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 16. Pantoprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 17. Phenobarbital decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 18. Phenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 19. Rabeprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 20. Rifampin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 21. Rifapentine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 22. St. John’s Wort decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 23. Vonoprazan decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Adagrasib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended. 25. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 26. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Rilpivirine and atidarsagene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least 1 month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 29. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Rilpivirine and betibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 31. Buprenorphine (all forms) and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Dofetilide increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Efavirenz and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Elivaldogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may interfere with each other. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least 1 month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications. 37. Encorafenib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Entrectinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Eribulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Fexinidazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 41. Rilpivirine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if QTc interval >500 ms or if there is a change from baseline >60 ms. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Lefamulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Rilpivirine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. 46. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin increases the corrected QT interval by ~11 ms. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 47. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir (DSC) increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with rilpivirine once daily is not recommended due to the potential for QT interval prolongation with higher rilpivirine concentrations. 48. Oxaliplatin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Ribociclib increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Rifabutin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, increase rilpivirine dose to 50 mg once daily. When rifabutin is stopped, decrease rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. 51. Sevoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Siponimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 53. Tetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Tovorafenib decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of efficacy. 55. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Exercise caution when co-administering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs. 56. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Exercise caution when co-administering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs. 57. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of amiodarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
